text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Security forces detained 10 Islamic Jihad activists in Hebron area.
- Newspapers in Damascus: threats by Israel's "Minister of War" must be taken seriously.
- Minister of interior: "The Jewish settlement in Hebron is not worth one drop of any soldier's blood".
- Labour and social affairs minister: number of job-seekers at three-year high.
JERUSALEM POST
- Government: Hebron talks backtracking.
- CIA agent charged with selling secrets to Russia.
- Knesset turmoil follows reports Peres advised Arafat.
- Ultra-orthodox radio stations ride a wave of popularity.
- El Al cuts 20% of planned winter timetable to pare losses.
- Histadrut to sell Hapoalim stake today.
- Tadiran net income up 8.5%.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Political storm over leak against Shimon Peres.
- Two border policemen suspended for beating Palestinians.
- Sources in Jerusalem estimate: Arafat is not interested in signing Hebron deal in near future.
MAARIV
- Two ultra-orthodox Jews tried to unearth bones of dead rabbi in Ukraine to bring to Israel.
GLOBES
- Rise in unemployment figures in October.
